name: Okta, Inc.

profile.description: Okta is the leading independent identity and access management platform, securing workforce and customer identities (Auth0) and, increasingly, AI agents via Okta for AI Agents and Auth0 for AI Agents. Co-founded in 2009 by CEO Todd McKinnon. Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026) revenue was $805M (+11%), subscription revenue $793M (+12%), RPO $4.858B (+17%) and free cash flow $227M; FY2027 revenue is guided to $3.216-3.226B (+10-11%). FY2026 revenue was $2.92B with GAAP net income of $235M. Market cap approximately $32B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Okta expanded from workforce identity into customer identity via Auth0 and is now extending into AI-agent identity, helping revenue compound from $835M (FY2021) to $2.92B (FY2026) [3]. AI Deployment (2/2): Okta for AI Agents, introduced in November 2025, had been purchased by dozens of companies and was in production at several by March 2026, alongside Auth0 for AI Agents [2]. Market Share (1/2): Okta is the leading independent identity platform, but Microsoft Entra is a larger bundled competitor and no share-gain data was found [2]. Product Pipeline (1/2): The AI-agent identity roadmap is named, but no revenue targets or dated launches beyond current products were disclosed [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FY2026 R&D of $639M is 21.9% of revenue, roughly in line with infrastructure-software peers rather than top quartile [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Okta's mission to free everyone to safely use any technology is specific and thoughtful, and its vendor-neutral strategy and push to secure AI agents trace directly back to it [2]; it falls short of 4 because the 2022 breach response — initially not disclosed, then downplayed — contradicted the trust the mission promises [5]. Community Impact (0/2): Our search did not surface specific, quantified community programs. Employee Retention (0/2): No tenure or turnover data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful insider open-market purchases were identified in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (10 weight units). D/E 0.76% scores 1.0 (1x) [4]. ROE 4.31% scores 0.29 (2x) [4]. Revenue growth YoY 10.6% scores 1.0 (1x) [4]. Revenue 5yr CAGR 28.4% (derived from FMP: $835M FY2021 to $2,919M FY2026) scores 1.0 (2x) [3]. Forward P/E 42.22 scores 0.44 (1x) [4]. Profit margin 9.63% scores 0.48 (1x) [4]. PEG 1.49 (Yahoo Finance) scores 0.76 (2x) [4]. Weighted sum = 1.0 + 0.57 + 1.0 + 2.0 + 0.44 + 0.48 + 1.51 = 7.01 / 10 → 7. Liquidity passes: 3.64M × $184.87 ≈ $673M/day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Identity is a control point AI makes more important, not less: management argues 'AI security is identity security', and Okta cites survey data that 91% of organizations already use AI agents while only 10% have a governance strategy [2]. The exposure is to AI-era pricing shifts — the 'SaaSpocalypse' debate over seat-based software that McKinnon has had to confront — and to Microsoft bundling identity into its AI stack, so it is protected rather than immune [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Okta for AI Agents has dozens of paying customers, but Okta has not disclosed AI-specific revenue figures, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded [2].

infinite_game.summary: Okta shows a mixed Sinek profile. Founder-CEO Todd McKinnon has held a consistent, vendor-neutral identity vision for 17 years and has extended it to AI agents, and the company made a hard turn from growth-at-all-costs losses to profitability. But the 2022 breach response revealed a reflex to protect the stock before customers, and competitive framing remains about owning the identity control point.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Free everyone to safely use any technology' is a genuine cause that has shaped strategy — a neutral platform integrating with all vendors, then customer identity, now AI-agent identity [2]. It has not yet been validated across decades or survived without contradiction, given the breach disclosure failures [5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong, with co-founder McKinnon CEO since 2009, and the company has delivered steady execution through its profitability pivot [2]. No retention or empowerment data was found, and operating expenses were held roughly flat ($2.06B to $2.11B) while revenue grew, consistent with cost discipline rather than evidence of exceptional trust [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management positions Okta as 'the world's system of record for identity management' and frames competition around owning that control point; no commentary acknowledging learning from rivals such as Microsoft was found [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Okta evolved from workforce SSO to customer identity (Auth0) and now non-human/AI-agent identity, and transformed its financial model from an $815M loss (FY2023) to $235M profit (FY2026) — meaningful adaptation within identity rather than abandoning a core business [2][3].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Okta committed to securing AI agents early, launching Okta for AI Agents in November 2025 before the market had a governance standard, and accepted a ~1-point growth headwind to shift professional services to partners [1][2]. The 2022 breach response — initially undisclosed, then downplayed — is a counterexample of protecting the short term [5].

investment_thesis: Okta has completed the turn from cash-burning growth to profitable compounding: FY2026 revenue of $2.92B produced $235M of GAAP net income versus an $815M loss three years earlier, TTM free cash flow is $1.04B, and the balance sheet holds $2.3B cash against just $53M of debt after settling the remaining 2026 notes for $350M in cash [1][3][4]. Revenue has compounded at a 28.4% CAGR from $835M in FY2021, and Q2 FY2027 RPO of $4.858B grew 17% — faster than revenue — signaling durable bookings [1][3]. Management's thesis that 'AI security is identity security' is gaining traction: Okta for AI Agents, launched in November, had been purchased by dozens of companies and was in production at several by March 2026, positioning Okta as the system of record for non-human identities [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is decelerating growth at a premium multiple. Revenue growth has slowed to 10-11% (Q3 FY2027 guided at ~10%, with a ~1-point headwind from shifting professional services to partners), yet the stock trades at 42.2x forward and 111x trailing earnings [1][4]. ROE is only 4.3% and GAAP profit margin 9.6% because stock-based compensation remains heavy [4]. Microsoft Entra bundling and seat-based pricing pressure in an AI-agent world (the so-called 'SaaSpocalypse' debate McKinnon has had to confront) threaten pricing power [2]. Okta's security credibility was damaged by the 2022 Lapsus$ breach — which it initially did not disclose and then downplayed, prompting a class action and a 15% stock drop — and any repeat would be severe for an identity vendor [5].
key_catalysts: AI-agent identity monetization: Okta for AI Agents and Auth0 for AI Agents scaling from 'dozens' of customers into a reported revenue line would re-rate growth expectations [2]
RPO acceleration: Q2 FY2027 RPO grew 17% to $4.858B versus 11% revenue growth — conversion of that backlog could lift reported growth above the 10-11% guide [1]
Capital return capacity: $1.04B TTM free cash flow and $2.3B cash with only $53M debt support buybacks and operating-margin expansion [4]
key_risks: Growth deceleration: Q3 FY2027 revenue guided at ~10% with cRPO growth of 11-12%, leaving a 42x forward P/E vulnerable if growth slips into single digits [1][4]
Platform competition and pricing: Microsoft Entra bundling and AI-agent-driven pressure on seat-based SaaS pricing could compress Okta's workforce identity business [2]

Breach/reputation risk: a repeat of the 2022 Lapsus$ incident — initially undisclosed, then downplayed, followed by a class action — would be especially damaging for a company whose product is trust [5]
